walkthroughs.body_html:
Crime & Punishment c1000-Present & Whitechapel c1870-1900 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Crime & Punishment c1000-Present & Whitechapel c1870-1900 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Crime & Punishment c1000-Present & Whitechapel c1870-1900.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Metropolitan Police in 1829?
options: William Gladstone
Robert Peel
Benjamin Disraeli
Lord Russell

mcqs.q: Where were most British convicts transported after 1787?
options: America
Australia
Canada
India

mcqs.q: How was crime punished in Anglo-Saxon England?
options: Through wergild ('man-price') compensation for victims, communal responsibility via tithings, trial by ordeal in disputed cases, and the death penalty for serious crimes.
The Bloody Code was a Tudor law against witchcraft.
Anglo-Saxons punished all crimes with imprisonment in castle dungeons.
Anglo-Saxons had no laws and just took revenge on each other.
The Bloody Code meant everyone caught for any crime was hanged immediately.
Peel created the police to fight the French during the Napoleonic Wars.
The 18th-century English legal system that made over 200 offences capital, intended as deterrence, but often softened by jury nullification and transportation to Australia.
The Bloody Code was a Tudor law against witchcraft.

mcqs.q: Why did Robert Peel create the Metropolitan Police in 1829?
options: The Bloody Code was a Tudor law against witchcraft.
Peel created the police because there had been no law enforcement of any kind before 1829.
Peel created the police to fight the French during the Napoleonic Wars.
Industrial London's crime, poor watchmen, and fear of disorder pushed Peel to create a professional, uniformed but unarmed force focused on crime prevention.
